patterns.label: Other provinces (2-3 digit area codes, all begin 02)

examples.note: Hanoi — area code 24 since the 2017 renumbering (was 4)
Ho Chi Minh City — area code 28 (was 8)
Mobile — 091 is a Vinaphone range; 096–098 Viettel, 090/093 MobiFone

notes: Vietnam renumbered in 2017–2018: landline area codes were re-prefixed so all now begin 02, and 11-digit mobile numbers on 012x/016x/018x/019x were converted to 10-digit numbers on 03x/05x/07x/08x.
Landline NSNs are 9–10 digits and mobile NSNs 9, so length alone is a weak validator.
Operator prefixes: 032–039 and 096–098 Viettel; 033–035, 091, 094 Vinaphone; 036–038, 090, 093 MobiFone.
sources: Ministry of Information and Communications: https://mic.gov.vn/

patterns.label: Provincial (2-digit area codes: 032 Phetchaburi, 053 Chiang Mai)

examples.note: Bangkok — area code 02 also covers nearby provinces
Chiang Mai — area code 053
Mobile — 08x, 09x and 06x ranges

notes: Thailand uses a closed plan: the area code must be dialled even for calls within the same area.
Bangkok has the single-digit area code 2 with a 7-digit subscriber number; provinces have 2-digit codes with 6-digit subscriber numbers.
1800 toll-free numbers are domestic-only and cannot be reached from abroad.
sources: NBTC — National Broadcasting and Telecommunications Commission: https://www.nbtc.go.th/

examples.note: Kuala Lumpur — area code 03, the largest block
Penang — area code 04
Mobile — 010–019 ranges

notes: Malaysia uses an open plan: landline area codes are 1–2 digits with 6–8 subscriber digits; mobile codes are 2 digits with 7–8 subscriber digits.
Until 2017 Singapore could be dialled from Malaysia as a domestic call using the 02 code; that arrangement ended and +65 international dialling is now required.
sources: MCMC — Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission: https://www.mcmc.gov.my/

examples.note: Fixed line — the 6 prefix covers PSTN and residential IP telephony
Mobile — 8 and 9 prefixes
Mobile — 8 prefix, including prepaid and data services

notes: Singapore has no area codes or trunk prefix — the country is a single numbering area. All numbers are 8 digits, adopted in 2002.
A 1800 toll-free number is an alias for a 6xxx xxxx line; from abroad you dial the underlying +65 6xxx xxxx number instead.
Until 1995 Singapore was dialled from Malaysia using a trunk prefix rather than a country code.
sources: IMDA — Infocomm Media Development Authority: https://www.imda.gov.sg/

examples.note: Fixed line — 2 and 3 prefixes
Fixed line — 3 prefix, generally newer allocations
Mobile — 4, 5, 6, 7 and 9 prefixes

notes: Hong Kong abolished area codes at the end of 1989; all numbers are a flat 8 digits with no trunk prefix.
The international access prefix is 001, not 00.
Hong Kong keeps its own country code +852 separate from mainland China's +86; calls between them are international.
sources: OFCA — Office of the Communications Authority: https://www.ofca.gov.hk/

examples.note: Fixed line — 28 is the main residential and business prefix
Fixed line — 8 prefix used by government and corporate lines
Mobile — all Macau mobiles begin with 6

notes: Macau has no area codes or trunk prefix; all numbers are 8 digits.
Macau keeps its own country code +853, separate from both mainland China (+86) and Hong Kong (+852).
sources: DSRT — Bureau of Telecommunications Regulation: https://www.dsrt.gov.mo/

examples.note: Taipei — area code 02 covers Taipei City, New Taipei City and Keelung
Taichung — area code 04
Mobile — all Taiwanese mobiles begin 09 and work nationwide
Toll-free — 0800 and 0809 prefixes

notes: The international access prefix varies by carrier (002, 005, 006, 007, 009), each billed differently.
Area codes are 1–2 digits after the trunk 0; Taipei is 2.

examples.note: Phnom Penh — area code 023
Mobile — 010 is a Smart Axiata range
Mobile — 088 is a Metfone range

notes: Cambodia uses a closed plan compliant with ITU-T E.164; the leading 0 is dropped when dialling from abroad.
The first two digits after the trunk 0 identify the operator for mobile numbers.
Mobile NSNs run 8–9 digits depending on the operator's allocated block.
sources: TRC — Telecommunication Regulator of Cambodia: https://trc.gov.kh/
